“As Columbus braved the seas, we now venture into the vast oceans of AGI. The age of AGI exploration has dawned, and the horizons are boundless. Dare to dream, dare to explore.” — α-AGI Agent

Abstract

An enterprise that explores the opportunity frontier needs both constructive imagination and a reliable way to discover when an attractive idea is already known. This study executes that combination. An adaptive search generated seven consequential opportunities absent from the supplied brief, screened them against primary prior art, and constructed two connected finite-model investigations of passive event-history memory. Exhaustive analysis exposes exactly when pairwise order records become ambiguous after an erasure. Classical parity repairs the abstract information loss, while a separate interacting-hysteron construction records two-event precedence with schedule-independent internal switching. Both constructions pass their declared computational checks. Neither establishes the substantive advance required for flagship selection: an ordinary library ties the parity construction, established monotone closure ties the hysteron construction, and the original four-event physical offering remains unqualified.

A conditional economic model makes the development decision concrete. Under favorable assumed demand, cost allowances and a 75% physical-qualification probability, the selected policy yields $417,868 mean annual operating profit conditional on qualification and $171,609 expected pre-tax project profit after central development cost. The customer action producing avoided loss and the completeness of real costs remain unvalidated. Central assumptions produce a $131,303 expected project loss; 137 of 512 favorable project worlds also lose money. Actual collections are zero and actual complete research expenditure is unknown. Native Insight, Nova-Seed, FusionPlan and authority workflows preserve the research while refusing unsupported venture promotion. The result is an executable, inspectable search boundary and a better specified next experiment. No candidate earns the flagship claim in this edition; beyond-human foresight, Operational Alpha and economically positive retained Alpha remain unestablished.

1. What becomes possible when capability can construct its own tests?

The productive ambition is to turn an overlooked possibility into a useful capability, an accepted outcome and a viable enterprise. A transformation must survive the strongest relevant existing approach, preserve the customer’s purpose and carry its costs. Agents can connect fields, construct executable objects and expose counterexamples; whether they discover opportunities beyond ordinary search is a separate empirical question.

This edition delivers a complete bounded research loop around a particularly revealing possibility: a material that preserves the order of events without a continuously powered logger. The search connected event-history memory, physical hysteresis and information recovery. Those connections were generated during the study; the user did not supply them as the answer. The decisive finding is that the initial information problem has an exact conventional repair, while the later physical abstraction has an exact conventional explanation. A promising story therefore becomes a documented rejection rather than an inflated invention claim. [1, 8–15, 31, 32]

The useful achievement combines executable acceptance boundaries, a same-offering commercial model and native workflows that preserve research while denying unsupported venture promotion. These improve the research record and its reproducibility; they do not constitute the requested headline breakthrough. [31–34]

The economic possibility is meaningful but conditional. In the favorable scenario, approximately 96,034 devices sold during twelve production months support $729,856 gross revenue and $417,868 operating profit after the modeled recurring costs. The same scenario requires physical qualification, sufficient buyer value and roughly $173,548 mean prefunding for development and peak operating credit. The physical product is unbuilt, actionable customer benefit and cost completeness are unvalidated, and the current decision is HOLD. Section 7 explains why positive operating economics can coexist with a negative development decision. [33]

2. An additive study within an existing research program

The repository and coordination issue were inspected before selecting a new study namespace. The audit records a repository snapshot at commit 47c17f6aca6b1bb8779dd3e47d5ba5f8af3329f4, inspected source hashes, current corrections and active ownership. Existing PEtab, manufacturing, microscopy, ecological, satellite and other occupied studies were treated as prior work rather than available flagship demonstrations. This study neither restarts those experiments nor imports their outcomes. [2, 35]

Three foundations shape the method. Transformational Intelligence separates useful purpose, formulation and evaluation: a transformation needs a witness showing how the changed formulation still serves the original purpose. Invent the Economy treats capability, counterparties, arrangements, rights and financing as distinct requirements. Autonomous Enterprises distinguishes retained money from productive capability and studies whether capabilities can be assembled into further work. These principles guide the present investigation; their experiments do not establish success here. [3–5]

The commercial studies also supply accounting discipline. Complete Economics of Accepted Work, Profitable Work First and When Paid Work Teaches the Network distinguish modeled delivery economics from actual collections and optional retention. The Network Learns to Invent contains a useful transfer result alongside a competent-control tie. The latest inspected Operational Alpha v2 study likewise records conventional parity, incomplete complete-cost evidence and zero collections. Those qualifications are retained rather than erased by a new narrative. No previous profit total, acceptance rate or transfer gain is credited to the present offering. [6, 7, 35]

The resulting selection rule has two independent gates. Origin: was the opportunity actually generated beyond what the initial brief supplied? Substantive advance: does the construction exceed identified prior art in a useful, testable respect under comparable obligations and resources? All seven serious candidates pass the first gate. None passes the second. Commercial usefulness could still justify a conventional service, but it would not meet this study’s flagship-discovery requirement.

3. Discovering the opportunity before choosing a demonstration

3.1 Search provenance and evidence boundaries

The exact initial brief is preserved in discovery/INITIAL_BRIEF.txt. The agent-generated record contains the beneficiary, valuable outcome, specific limitation, changed capability, proposed connection, construction, falsifier, commercial mechanism and successor inheritance for every serious candidate. The discovery-agent subtask involved 31 query strings across nine search requests and six direct page opens. These retrospective counts exclude other team searches and were not preregistered limits. [1, 31]

Initial digital candidates encountered close prior art. The search then broadened into temporal and material mechanisms, partly in response to coordination messages identifying occupied research lanes. This steering is preserved as researcher input. It was not a blind comparison against ordinary frontier-model search. No human expert search, independent provider-controlled U/E experiment or historical replay occurred. Search results, newly found papers and later refinements were visible to the investigators. Absence from a small candidate sample therefore supports no claim that humans could not have conceived an opportunity.

4. A connected example with an unchanged useful purpose

The original offering is a hypothetical passive chronology device: after four distinct physical events have each occurred once, a customer reads the retained state and recovers the complete event order, even when one readout bit is known to be missing. The useful outcome is reliable history, not merely detection that an event occurred. Potential beneficiaries are operators for whom a missed sequence changes an actionable decision; the economic model represents such buyers without asserting that any specific organization has agreed to buy.

The transformation witness makes the obligation explicit. The restriction is that ordinary pairwise order readouts can become ambiguous after an erasure. The proposed change is to encode additional information into the stored state. Preserved obligations include all 24 four-event histories, a declared erasure location, correct surviving bits, the same final-readout purpose and complete component accounting. Acceptance requires unique recovery and, for the commercial offering, a realizable physical implementation with qualified reliability and cost. Any pair of permitted histories sharing the surviving readout falsifies the recovery claim. [31]

A two-event latch cannot become a four-event erasure-tolerant product by changing the wording of the result.

5. Exact information recovery: a useful construction with conventional parity

5.1 Why the original record fails

For nn distinct, exactly-once events, encode a permutation using all m=n(n−1)/2m=n(n-1)/2 pairwise precedence bits. A bit records whether one named event preceded another. All bits together identify the permutation. However, exchanging two adjacent events changes exactly their mutual comparison and leaves every other pairwise comparison unchanged. The resulting code therefore has minimum Hamming distance one. Every history has at least one vulnerable erasure. This is an elementary argument, not a claim of a new coding theorem. [12, 31]

For a fixed history, precisely n−1n-1 of its mm pairwise comparisons join adjacent events. Erasing one of these comparisons leaves the two neighboring orders indistinguishable. Erasing a nonadjacent comparison leaves a chain of intervening events that implies it. Under a uniform choice of the erased pair, the exact ambiguous fraction is therefore 2/n2/n, and the uniquely recoverable fraction is 1−2/n1-2/n. This distributional statement differs from a worst-case guarantee: the bare code fails that guarantee at every tested size. [31]

A four-cycle pairwise graph produces only 14 distinct readouts for 24 histories. All six pairwise comparisons distinguish all 24 intact histories, but uniquely recover only 72 of 144 history/erasure cases. This abstract graph calculation is not a correction to the mechanics or experimental claims of the published periodic metamaterial. It isolates a declared information model inspired by that literature. [8, 31]

Figure 1. Exhaustive abstract-code results. Bare pairwise records recover 50%, 60% and 66.67% of uniformly enumerated single-erasure cases at n = 4, 5 and 6. Standard XOR parity recovers all declared cases. The conventional identical-information library comparator ties on the new-size checks; a separate bitset oracle independently verifies the saved recovery sets. These are finite computations, not physical-device reliability measurements.

5.2 Repair, resource bounds and negative cases

Append one bit equal to the XOR of the mm pairwise bits. When one known bit is erased, the surviving parity equation determines it; if parity itself is erased, the original pairwise record remains intact. At four events, the augmented abstract code recovers all 168 history/erasure cases. This is classical parity applied to a new research connection. Its correctness does not make the coding principle novel. [12, 31]

A duplication baseline requires 2m2m stored bits within the restricted class that stores only copies of individual pairwise comparisons. Every pair can be adjacent in some history, so each must have at least two copies to survive an arbitrary single erasure. The parity code uses m+1m+1 logical bits. This comparison counts logical readouts; it is not a lower bound for arbitrary encodings or a proof of lower physical cost. A physical parity element could require couplers, ancillas, routing, fabrication tolerances, energy or readout mechanisms absent from the logical count.

Figure 2. ABCD and BACD differ only in the AB comparison. Removing that comparison makes their bare readouts identical. An additional conventional parity bit separates the two abstract codewords. The diagram identifies the information requirement; it does not supply a fabricated parity mechanism.

The source and configuration were frozen before fresh-size enumeration. At five events, bare recovery is 720/1,200 versus parity recovery of 1,320/1,320. At six events, the corresponding results are 7,200/10,800 and 11,520/11,520. The denominators differ because the augmented code has one additional erasable position. A separate bitset-intersection implementation checked all 198,840 enumerated recovery cases without disagreement; another check verified 24,000 duplication cases. The ordinary library containing the identical coding information ties on all 12,840 single-erasure cases at the new sizes. [31]

The preserved failures delimit the result. With two erasures, 1,560 of 6,600 five-event cases and 13,680 of 86,400 six-event cases remain ambiguous under parity. All 12,840 tested single-bit substitutions are detected, but a single parity check cannot generally correct an unknown flipped bit. Erasing parity while flipping AB can silently change ABCDE(F) into BACDE(F); flipping AB and AC can produce BCADE(F) with parity still satisfied. These cases lie outside the promised one-known-erasure model and are retained so that successors cannot quietly generalize the guarantee.

The new-size checks establish implementation consistency on fresh finite tasks. The general coding argument and the four-event design were already known before their execution. Accordingly, this is technical transfer of a known procedure, not learned independent competence, prospective foresight or numerical retained Alpha.

6. A second construction: deterministic internal races, order-sensitive inputs

6.1 Exact hysteron model

The next search refinement sought a physically interpretable distinction: internal switching order should not alter the result, while the order of external events should. The constructed model contains binary states sis_i, a held input vector hh, and effective fields

Hi(s,h)=hi+∑jCijsj. H_i(s,h)=h_i+\sum_j C_{ij}s_j.

An inactive bit may switch on when Hi≥1.00H_i\geq1.00; an active bit may switch off when Hi≤−0.80H_i\leq-0.80. Every allowed single-bit update choice is explored. No update priority is used to manufacture determinism. Nominal calculations use exact integer-scaled values. [32]

For the four-bit state (x,y,z,w)(x,y,z,w), only Cxz=Czx=0.60C_{xz}=C_{zx}=0.60 and Cyw=Cwy=0.60C_{yw}=C_{wy}=0.60 are nonzero. Pulse A is (1.20,0,0,0.60)(1.20,0,0,0.60), and pulse B is (0,1.20,0.60,0)(0,1.20,0.60,0). Each is held until settling and followed by zero input. C holds A+B simultaneously; R applies (−2,−2,−2,−2)(-2,-2,-2,-2) until settling and then returns to zero. Two- and three-bit projections are evaluated as separate models. An independent Boolean recurrence supplies the semantic oracle:

x′=x∨a,y′=y∨b,z′=z∨[b∧(x∨a)],w′=w∨[a∧(y∨b)]. x'=x\lor a,\quad y'=y\lor b,\quad z'=z\lor[b\land(x\lor a)],\quad w'=w\lor[a\land(y\lor b)].

R clears the state. Under the declared exactly-once two-event interpretation, AB produces 1110 and BA produces 1101. C, ABA and BAB all produce 1111. The collisions are central: the model cannot reconstruct full history or uniquely identify simultaneous events. Arbitrary finite-duration overlaps, thermal activation and physical switching dynamics are outside its settled-input abstraction. [32]

Figure 3. Four-bit abstract hysteron readouts distinguish AB from BA, while C, ABA and BAB collide at 1111. Every allowed internal update schedule agrees within the declared model. A conventional monotone-closure implementation gives identical results. This partial event-order construction does not satisfy the original four-event single-erasure offering.

6.2 Why it works, and why it does not earn novelty

Under A, B, C and zero, an active bit cannot switch off because fields are nonnegative and the off threshold is negative. Every on-switch can only increase neighboring fields. The process is therefore monotone on a finite Boolean lattice and reaches the same least fixed point under every maximal asynchronous update sequence. R forces all bits off. With symmetric couplings, the coarse energy

E(s;h)=−∑ihisi−∑i<jCijsisj E(s;h)=-\sum_i h_i s_i-\sum_{i<j}C_{ij}s_i s_j

strictly decreases at every allowed fixed-input switch. This supports finite-model consistency; it supplies neither a continuous elastic energy landscape nor a manufactured device. Different external vector paths can still yield different final states. Internal confluence does not imply that AB and BA commute, and this result does not overturn scalar return-point-memory theory. [13, 32]

The confirmation includes all 140 nominal initial-state/held-field cases across two, three and four bits; 5,461 words of length zero through six per model over A/B/C/R; and 1,024 fresh seeded words of length one through 64 per model. There are no oracle disagreements or nominal nonconfluent cases. Parameter checks use 512 draws per dimension, perturbing present symmetric edges, thresholds and nonzero drives by at most 0.04, giving 71,680 state/field checks without disagreement. Analytic interval margins also cover the continuous specified perturbation box; the smallest required gated-activation margin is 0.08. These are model checks, not independent physical trials or estimated real failure rates. [32]

Unfavorable controls remain executable. Reducing each coupling from 0.60 to 0.35 destroys order discrimination. An antagonistic pair terminates in either 01 or 10 depending on update order. An asymmetric feedback pair cycles. The checker reports these behaviors. Eight acceptance tests pass, including the negative controls.

The novelty verdict follows from stronger comparisons. Conventional monotone closure matches the proposed dynamics exactly. Mechanical counting, pattern recognition and reset already exist; systematic transition-graph synthesis already exists; vectorial sequential memory and autonomous event-order recorders are identified prior art. The autonomous recorder comparison is especially useful because its first-occurrence semantics are different from, and in some respects stronger than, this recurrent-precedence state. Direct full text was unavailable for the recent vectorial-memory preprint, so no detailed performance comparison to it is asserted. A working threshold motif earns a reference construction, not a new discovery claim. [9, 10, 13–15, 32]

7. Commercial delivery, pricing and financing for the same offering

7.1 Scope and calibrated assumptions

The commercial model concerns the original physically qualified four-event chronology device with one known erased readout. It does not sell the smaller latch, the abstract code or a generic diagnostic service. There is no equivalent human-service market price to halve. Instead, the comparison estimates a human-led development pathway and models buyer value separately. All buyers, volumes, physical success probabilities, device costs and prices are explicit scenarios; none is a quote, sale or demonstrated willingness to pay. [33]

Two external anchors calibrate development labor. Job Bank reports Montréal mechanical-engineer wages of CAD 30.43, 44.52 and 66.39 per hour, with a 2024 reference period and a 19 November 2025 update. The Bank of Canada’s retrieved 26 October 2026 indicative rate is CAD 1.4025 per USD. Loading assumptions of 1.45, 1.70 and 2.10 produce USD 31.46, 53.96 and 99.41 per engineering hour. The loading factors, hours and other costs are planning estimates, not source-reported project costs. [26, 27, 33]

Assumed duration 3 months 9 months 18 months
Human-led total H $37,447 $141,170 $576,411
Expert AI, no labor benefit E0 $38,054 $141,792 $577,056

Physical test labor is costed at assumed USD 32, 45 and 65 per hour. Research financing uses 10% annually on an assumed average half-deployed balance over the stated duration. Fifteen percent of engineering cost represents failed screens already inside the total. The central E0 total consists of $48,567 engineering, $22,500 physical testing, $65,000 external work, $600 inference/tools and $5,125 financing. The $600 is a scenario allowance: 20 million input and four million output tokens at the documented gpt-6-astra rates yield $400, plus $200 tools and compute. It is not a provider invoice. [28, 33]

E0 assumes no AI reduction in engineering hours or increase in physical success. Hypothetical 25% and 50% engineering-hour reductions are sensitivities, with physical testing unchanged. A high human R&D estimate therefore cannot silently become evidence that an AI pathway is cheaper, faster or more likely to work.

7.2 Buyer participation and the best tested arrangement

For each simulated buyer, device value combines assumed avoided losses and staff savings, less false-alarm costs. The model assigns 70% prevented-loss benefit, but a passive record read after an event cannot undo its damage. A downstream decision—such as disposition, future prevention or adjudication—and its timing must be specified before this becomes calibrated value. A manual outside option receives its own assumed loss avoidance, staff saving and $3 per-unit cost. Incremental value is the positive difference between device value and the best modeled outside option. Buyers participate only when effective price plus the financing cost of any deposit is at most 70% of that incremental value. The remaining surplus supplies an explicit participation margin; the rule is an assumption, not an elicited demand curve or a truthful mechanism. [33]

The tested list-price grid is $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $8, $10, $12, $16 and $20. Payment policies are net 30 or a 20% deposit with a 5% price discount. Deposit financing is charged to buyers at an assumed 10% annual rate for thirty days. The supplier’s credit-loss model distinguishes postpaid exposure. A lower effective price can increase participation while a deposit reduces financing pressure; raising prices never holds demand artificially fixed.

Development uses 128 worlds. Policies were saved before a fresh confirmation seed generated 512 worlds for each of three scenarios. Capacity is capped at 120,000 devices annually. Potential buyers number 18, 40 or 70, with central per-buyer volumes of 2,000, 3,000 or 3,500 respectively; reachability, buyer value, demand, volume and unit cost vary under the declared distributions. The selected policies are the best tested policies for this model and grid, not globally optimal real-world prices. [33]

Unit production cost is decomposed into materials 40%, fabrication 25%, quality assurance 15%, packaging/shipping 12%, and support/recovery 8%. These are broad allowances, not an evidenced complete bill of materials. Failed-prospect effort, yield/rework, equipment, qualification, rights, insurance and exceptional returns are unscoped. The 8% support/recovery allocation may overlap the separate warranty charge; internal physical-test labor and external testing also lack task-level separation. Arithmetic consistency cannot establish that real costs are complete or counted once. Fixed overhead and acquisition are separate model entries. The twelve-month delivery model includes a thirteenth month for receivable and warranty runoff. Deposits, production and assumed acceptance occur sequentially within a monthly bucket. The thirty-day lead is a buyer opportunity-cost assumption, not dated seller cash evidence. Deposits become revenue only at assumed acceptance; credit principal is financing, not revenue. Warranty expense is 2% of revenue, while a distinct 3% liquidity reserve affects available cash without being expensed twice. [33]

A revolving facility at an assumed 10% annual rate covers operating cash deficits. In the favorable case, mean peak credit is $31,756. Adding central development gives mean capital required of $173,548, with a ninety-fifth percentile of $179,382. These are period-end requirements under coarse monthly timing, not committed capital: intramonth peaks, procurement leads, sales ramps, refunds and delayed acceptance are unresolved. Actual collections, deliveries, recognized revenue and token receipts are all zero. The actual full attributable session cost is unknown, so no actual profit or available growth fund is asserted. [33, 34]

7.4 Robustness, losses and the development decision

At the favorable base assumptions, the break-even qualification probability is approximately 0.339. This threshold holds the modeled operating distribution and central development cost fixed. Central operating economics would require q>1q>1 to repay that development cost within the modeled horizon. Higher R&D costs can overturn the favorable case: the high E0 development estimate produces approximately −$263,655 expected project profit; even an assumed 50% engineering-hour reduction leaves it negative. [33]

An exploratory demand/cost grid keeps the selected policies fixed. Twenty-four of 42 favorable grid cells have both positive expected project profit and a positive fifth-percentile annual operating profit; no central or conservative cell does. At half base demand and unchanged unit cost, favorable annual operating profit remains approximately $160,565, yet expected project profit becomes −$21,368. At 75% demand and 1.5 times unit cost, expected project profit is about $41,179. These bounds clarify which economic assumptions deserve early calibration. They are not a demonstrated robust market region. [33]

A same-team independent Decimal audit checked 16,968 identities or comparisons across all 1,536 confirmation worlds; the saved reconstructed auditor adds 12,543 numeric checks. Residuals remain below $0.000001. The original inline command was not preserved; its reconstructed source and changed rounding residual are explicitly documented. This validates arithmetic, failure preservation and physical-work invariance, not actionable benefit, real cost completeness or disjoint cost scope. The model-review record preserves these material limitations without changing the frozen results. [33] All actual decisions remain HOLD: unqualified physical offering and failed novelty gate. Avoiding future expenditure does not erase sunk research cost.

7.5 Post-result cost headroom

An additional exploratory accounting stress, performed after the frozen results, asks how much unscoped cost the favorable case could absorb without changing buyer behavior, prices, qualification or financing. Let ΔA\Delta A be additional originating cost and ΔO\Delta O additional annual qualified-operation expense. Positive expected project profit requires ΔA+0.75ΔO<171,608.78\Delta A+0.75\Delta O<171{,}608.78 USD. Keeping its fifth-percentile annual operating result positive additionally requires ΔO<191,951.16\Delta O<191{,}951.16 USD for a constant annual expense. The central case has no nonnegative added-cost region. These are accounting boundaries inside the constructed scenario, not estimates of omitted costs, evidence of cost completeness or a behavioral reoptimization. Induced financing, delays and demand responses require a new model. The exact derivation and provenance are in results/cost-headroom-exploratory.json and src/cost_headroom.py. Actual HOLD is unchanged. [33]

claude-fable-5-1 Independent-family validation candidate Adaptive thinking, max, 64,000 cap 10 / 50
claude-opus-5-5 Implementation comparator Adaptive thinking, high, 64,000 cap 4 / 20
gemini-4-argon Scientific reasoning candidate high, 65,536 output cap 2 / 10 through 30 November 2026

The inventory records context limits, selected provider tool availability and the Google rate change scheduled for December. The listed configurations are proposals, not executed mission configurations; exact tool schema versions must be frozen before a comparative provider run. OpenAI reasoning/tool proposals use the Responses API and omit unsupported sampling controls. Actual cost logs must include reasoning output, retries, verification and tool usage. Closed weights, unrestricted consumer-subscription automation and untested account access are not assumed.

Operational Alpha means E performing better than U with the same frontier model, initial evidence, tools, reasoning limits and total budget. Retained Alpha compares E+ with E after charging the incremental retained capability. The present study implements expert research practices—source construction, decomposition, exact verification, adversarial controls and recovery—but contains no controlled numerical E-versus-U result. H is a transparent development estimate, not a recruited human team. Independent implementations were produced within the same assistant-controlled team; they are not independent model families or blinded human adjudicators. [31–35]

A prospective comparison should therefore be frozen before its next discovery run. The proposed design uses identical need/resource packets containing no intended opportunity, source access cutoffs, equal model identifiers and monetary/token limits, and a fixed candidate budget. Representative U receives a competent open-ended opportunity-search instruction and the same available tools; E receives the expert orchestration procedure. Expertise may change decomposition and verification, but cannot obtain extra information or budget. Multiple sessions and seed assignments should be specified in the frozen protocol, rather than selected after favorable outputs appear.

Novelty, usefulness, technical feasibility and commercial plausibility should be reviewed separately against predeclared criteria. Reviewers should receive source-backed constructions without condition labels where practical. Human experts should search the same packet if recruited; otherwise the edition must report that the human comparison is absent or explicitly modeled. The final test must include an executable construction or decisive experiment, with fresh acceptance cases hidden from the search sessions. Merely failing to mention an opportunity in a baseline sample does not establish beyond-human foresight. Historical replay would additionally require defensible information cutoffs and leakage controls; none is claimed here.

9. Insight, Nova-Seed, FusionPlan and MARK as an actual connected mechanism

The integration copies and hashes forty unchanged adapter source/license files and two additional unchanged scenario modules from the audited repository snapshot. It executes native scenario analysis, Nova-Seed cryptographic roundtripping, FusionPlan compilation and verification, cost-ledger safeguards, and authority checks. This is a real local integration with public fixtures, distinct from a narrative business plan. [34, 35]

The native Insight scenario receives seven reviewer-supplied rejected candidates and retrieves eight exact excerpts from their supplied evidence. Each candidate has unit synthetic cost and zero eligibility value. Across 128 possible subsets it selects none, produces no schedule, and makeGenome refuses to create a venture genome. Identical numeric coordinates place all seven candidates on the computed nondominated frontier, which does not make them qualified. The numeric setup records the completed review; it is not an independent semantic novelty evaluation or proof that Insight discovered the rejection unaided. The generic refusal suggestion to increase budget does not override the actual reason: eligibility is zero despite every candidate fitting the synthetic budget.

A separate research Nova-Seed preserves the negative result, opportunity, original purpose, sources, uncertainty, rights scope, transformation witness, evidence and next experiment. Native WebCrypto encryption and authenticated decryption roundtrip the object; wrong passphrases and modified commitments are rejected. A public fixture passphrase establishes an inspectable test, not secrecy. Cryptographic integrity shows that the object is unchanged, not that its scientific claim is true.

The FusionPlan contains four executable milestone descriptions: discovery, construction, economics and retention. Native Merkle compilation and verification check committed fields. The fixture allocates 100 base units of AGIALPHA per job, 400 total; these are local test units, not USD, funded bounties or revenue. Dependencies, full budgets, permissions, acceptance conditions and falsifiers are retained in the research object. The native commitment format does not itself enforce every wider research obligation.

Thirteen adapter checks pass. They include rejecting a substituted acceptance metric, double-charged activities, treating unknown cost as zero, unsupported capsule scope, unreviewed rights and production admission based only on a valid local signature. A simulated identity without live ENS authorization remains denied, and denial does not consume the challenge. The public research artifact cannot be renamed to fit an existing production capability’s narrower approved scope. The adapter emits an inspectable MARK review packet; MARK execution remains NOT_EXECUTED, and no minting, listing, trading, funds movement, on-chain action or expanded permission occurs. [34]

These outcomes preserve the existing validator roles. The research pipeline can archive a useful failed hypothesis while venture promotion and production access remain closed. Native execution used Python 3.12.14 and Node 24.22.1; the production Node pin differs, so the local checks are not a production release qualification.

10. What the successor inherits—and what it must earn

The successor can inherit exact models, source-scoped claims, counterexamples, configurations, a schedule-complete checker, an independent decoding oracle and the complete commercial assumptions. Each object has a version, provenance, dependencies, scope and failure modes. The intended rights scope is public research code and public-source metadata; external publications retain their own rights. Secrets, customer material and protected evaluation answers are not part of the capsule. [31–35]

Accounting separates A, originating delivery or research; B, additional evaluation, extraction, retention, invocation and maintenance; and C, optional extra research or Gym training. Necessary learning already charged to A is not charged again in B. The present construction was unpaid research, not learning acquired during an accepted paid job. The actual native ledger marks originating and additional-validation expenditure unknown, sets optional Gym execution to zero, and refuses to calculate actual profit from incomplete costs.

The optional retained-service scenario adds $2,500 extraction/validation and $1,200 annual maintenance, or $3,700. Ten future missions would require an average $370 incremental benefit per mission to break even. The identical-information ordinary library produces no observed acceptance improvement over the retained code. Under the tested zero-incremental-saving case, the optional premium retention investment loses $3,700 and is rejected. Public preservation remains useful; it is not evidence that maintaining a specialist business is free or profitable. [33]

No model weights were trained, no Gym learning curve was measured and no specialist superhuman claim is made. The fresh five- and six-event tasks demonstrate the same known algorithm operating at new sizes. Remote service access would likewise not establish that a recipient independently acquired competence. The operational inheritance rule is: REUSE stable structure; RECHECK the new mission’s meaning; REGRANT authority separately. Authenticated agent-network distribution must use the actual authorization workflow; local fixture identities do not grant access across *.agent.agi.eth.

The next challenge is a useful physical history property that existing mechanical, finite-state and coding controls cannot satisfy under the same complete resource budget. The inherited models help falsify proposals; they do not establish that such a gap exists.

11. The smallest useful next validation

The first next step is a bounded novelty-and-realizability challenge, before a full hardware program. Specify one valuable history predicate, its event and fault model, complete physical component budget, permissible energy and readout mechanism. Ask a materials specialist to compare it with the identified general hysteron-synthesis, event-recorder and classical-code controls. A proposed advantage fails if a conventional construction meets the same obligations at comparable total resources.

If a functional gap survives, map the smallest motif to a calibrated continuous potential or existing tunable-hysteron geometry. Check metastable branches, actual ramps, damping, noise and reset; then fabricate only the component needed to falsify the proposed physical mechanism. This step would test physical feasibility. Fabricating the already known parity or latch principle alone would not repair the novelty deficit. The complete four-event erasure requirement remains the product acceptance gate.

In parallel, a small scoped buyer interview can test whether the claimed history changes a real decision, what outside option is used, and whether the favorable model’s incremental value and volume assumptions are plausible. A quote can calibrate fabrication and test costs. These activities refine a conditional model; they do not retroactively turn simulated revenue into collections. Their budgets and permissions must be separately authorized when needed.

The exact constructions, conventional ties and rejected opportunities equip a successor to continue the search with its acceptance standard intact.
